title: John Perry Barlow
name: John Perry Barlow
summary: American writer and activist who co-founded the Electronic Frontier Foundation and wrote 'A Declaration of the Independence of Cyberspace'.
whyThisMatters: Barlow framed the early Internet as a civil-liberties frontier and helped create the organization that has defended hackers and researchers in court ever since.
knownFor: A Declaration of the Independence of Cyberspace (1996)

sections.overview:
John Perry Barlow was an American poet, essayist, and activist, and a lyricist for the Grateful Dead. In 1990, after being questioned by the FBI during the investigations that followed Operation Sundevil, he wrote Crime and Puzzlement, describing how poorly law enforcement understood computer networks.

The EFF

That year he co-founded the Electronic Frontier Foundation with Mitch Kapor and John Gilmore to defend civil liberties online, beginning with support for hackers and companies swept up in the Sundevil raids. Barlow is credited with popularizing the term "cyberspace" for the Internet.

The Declaration

On 8 February 1996, responding to the U.S. Telecommunications Act, Barlow published A Declaration of the Independence of Cyberspace from Davos, declaring that governments had no sovereignty over the networked world. He was a fellow at Harvard's Berkman Center and co-founded the Freedom of the Press Foundation in 2012. He died in February 2018.
